title: GST 121 ( UNIZIK ) : LAW AND THE REGULATION OF HUMAN CONDUCT IN SOCIETY
subject: GST 121

questions.question: Society is described as a collection of individuals interacting to achieve which goal?
questions.explanation: The society is a collection of individuals interacting among themselves in order to achieve a common goal.

questions.question: The interaction of individuals in society often leads to which outcome?
questions.explanation: The interaction in society is not without some forms of conflicts resulting from the competing interests of the individuals.

questions.question: Law is described as which part of a civilized society?
questions.explanation: Law is the lifeline of every civilized society as it sets out a standard of conduct for the common good.

questions.question: The statement that man is a gregarious animal implies humans are naturally which of the following?
questions.explanation: Man is a gregarious animal and universally lives with his fellowman, indicating a social nature.

questions.question: In Hindu culture, law implies which term?
questions.explanation: In Hindu, law implies Dharma.

questions.question: In Islamic culture, law means which term?
questions.explanation: In Islam, law means Hokum.

questions.question: To the Romans, law means which term?
questions.explanation: To the Romans, law means Jus.

questions.question: According to Roscoe Pound, the definition of law has been the battleground of whom?
questions.explanation: Roscoe Pound observed that the definition of law has been the battleground of jurists.

questions.question: Salmond defines law as the body of principles recognized and applied by the state in the administration of which concept?
questions.explanation: Salmond defines law as the body of principles recognized and applied by the state in the administration of justice.

questions.question: John Austin defines law as a command backed by which element?
questions.explanation: John Austin defines law as a command set by a superior being to inferior beings and enforced by sanctions.

questions.question: Oliver Wendell Holmes defines law as the prophecies of what the courts will do in which context?
questions.explanation: Oliver Wendell Holmes defines law as the prophecies of what the courts will do, in fact and nothing more pretentious.

questions.question: Thomas Aquinas defines law as an ordinance of reason for which purpose?
questions.explanation: For Thomas Aquinas, law is an ordinance of reason for the common good.

questions.question: The characteristic of law that sets a standard of conduct is known as which term?
questions.explanation: Law is normative as it is a set of rules that prescribes what is to be done and prohibits certain acts.

questions.question: Law-making power at the federal level in Nigeria is vested on which body?
questions.explanation: In Nigeria, law-making power is vested on the National Assembly at the federal level and States Houses of Assembly at the state level.

questions.question: The positivist argument that sanction makes a rule a law is associated with which theorist?
questions.explanation: Positivist theorists like John Austin argued that sanction is an important character of law.

questions.question: Wills Law and Sales of Goods Act are examples of laws that are not which of the following?
questions.explanation: Wills Law and Sales of Goods Act are not coercive in nature, contradicting the strict positivist view.

questions.question: Law operates within the context of which entity?
questions.explanation: Law does not exist in a vacuum but exists within the context of the society.

questions.question: The characteristic of law that allows it to change according to the needs of society is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law is dynamic because it changes from time to time according to the needs of the society.

questions.question: Which theory is the oldest school of thought in law?
questions.explanation: Natural Law theory is the oldest theory of law.

questions.question: The principle that an unjust law is not law belongs to which school of thought?
questions.explanation: Natural theorists posit that any law which does not conform to natural tenets is unjust, and an unjust law is not law.

questions.question: Which theory posits that law is the command of the sovereign?
questions.explanation: For the positivist school of thought, law is the command of the sovereign.

questions.question: Which scholar is the major proponent of the sociological theory of law?
questions.explanation: The major proponent of the sociological theory is Roscoe Pound.

questions.question: The theory that perceives law as an instrument of social engineering is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The sociological school perceives law as an instrument of social engineering by which conflicting interests are balanced.

questions.question: The functional theory of law is majorly associated with which scholar?
questions.explanation: The major proponent of the functional theory of law is Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.

questions.question: Friedrich Carl Von Savigny is the major proponent of which theory?
questions.explanation: Friedrich Carl Von Savigny is the major proponent of the historical theory of law.

questions.question: According to the historical theory, law proceeds from the custom of a people known as which term?
questions.explanation: According to the historical school, law proceeds from the custom or volkgeist of a people.

questions.question: Jeremy Bentham is the major proponent of which theory of law?
questions.explanation: Jeremy Bentham is a major proponent of the utilitarian school of law.

questions.question: According to the utilitarian school, the most important basic utility is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The utilitarian school recognizes security as the most important of the basic utilities.

questions.question: Common Law is the local laws applicable to English communities after which event?
questions.explanation: The Common Law is the local laws applicable to the English communities following the Norman Conquest of 1066 AD.

questions.question: The doctrines of equity were developed by which court?
questions.explanation: The doctrines of equity developed from the Chancery court as a result of the rigidity of the Common Law rules.

questions.question: Which Act merged the principles of Common Law and equity?
questions.explanation: By the Judicature Act of 1875, the principles of Common Law and that of equity were merged.

questions.question: Statutes of General Application are laws in force in England on which date?
questions.explanation: Statutes of General Application are those laws that were in force in England on the 1st day of January, 1900.

questions.question: Laws enacted by the National Assembly at the federal level are known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: At the federal level, laws enacted by the National Assembly are known as an Act while it is called a Law at the state level.

questions.question: The doctrine where lower courts are bound by higher court decisions is called which term?
questions.explanation: The doctrine of judicial precedents draws from the doctrine of stare decisis where lower courts are bound by the principles of the judgement of a higher court.

questions.question: To be enforceable in Nigeria, a custom must pass how many validity tests?
questions.explanation: To be enforceable, a custom must pass three validity tests: repugnancy, incompatibility, and public policy.

questions.question: Which source of law governs the conduct of Muslims in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Sharia law is a set of rules and regulations that governs the conduct of Muslims.

questions.question: The branch of law that regulates the relationship between the state and persons is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Public law is a branch of law which regulates the relationship between the state and persons making up the state.

questions.question: Crimes committed against the State are prosecuted by the State under which branch of law?
questions.explanation: Criminal law stipulates, forbids, and punishes crimes which are committed against the State and prosecuted by the State.

questions.question: Which law is applicable to southern Nigeria regarding crimes?
questions.explanation: In Nigeria, crime is regulated by the Criminal Code Act applicable to southern Nigeria and the Penal Code Act applicable to northern Nigeria.

questions.question: Felonies are crimes punishable by death or imprisonment of not less than how many years?
questions.explanation: Felonies are punishable by death or a term of imprisonment of 3 years and above.

questions.question: The legal system where an alleged criminal is presumed innocent until proven guilty is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Common law legal system uses the adversarial system of justice where an alleged criminal is presumed innocent until a court says so.

questions.question: Which legal system applies the inquisitorial system of justice?
questions.explanation: The Civil Law legal system applies the inquisitorial system of justice where an alleged criminal is deemed guilty until he proves otherwise.

questions.question: Substantive law defines rights and duties, while procedural law is also known as which term?
questions.explanation: Procedural law is also known as adjectival or remedial law.

questions.question: The most basic and elementary function of law in society is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Social regulation is the most basic and elementary function of law in society.

questions.question: Which philosopher posits that the function of law is the maximization of happiness?
questions.explanation: Jeremy Bentham posits that the function of law is the maximization of the happiness of the greatest number of members of the society.

questions.question: According to Lon Fuller, the function of law is to guide which concept?
questions.explanation: Lon Fuller asserts that the function of law is to guide human conduct.

questions.question: Law serves as an instrument of social engineering by balancing which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law serves as an instrument of social engineering by which conflicting interests are balanced.

questions.question: The concept of social control is attributed to which scholar?
questions.explanation: The use of the concept of social control has been attributed to Roscoe Pound when he described law as a specialized form of social control.

questions.question: Which technique of social control involves the use of rules that prohibit unacceptable acts and provide sanctions?
questions.explanation: The penal technique involves the use of rules which prohibits certain unacceptable acts and the provision of sanctions for non-compliance.

questions.question: Which technique provides a legal framework for agreements between specific individuals, such as marriage?
questions.explanation: The private arranging technique provides a legal framework which determines the status of arrangements and agreements between persons, such as marriage or making a Will.
